note.question: Why are microinfluencers often more selective than celebrities, and how do the informativeness of follower comments and the cost of reading them affect an influencer's endorsement policy, a seller's prices, consumer learning, and joint endorsement profit?
note.overview: The paper derives a perfect Bayesian equilibrium in which an influencer commits to an endorsement policy, a privately informed seller-influencer pair conditions participation on product quality, the seller sets prices, and sequential consumer cohorts purchase, comment, and learn. Endorsement selectivity and prices are strategic equilibrium choices.

components.label: Perfect Bayesian equilibrium
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Perfect Bayesian equilibrium. Section 4 explicitly names perfect Bayesian equilibrium as the solution concept and requires correct on-path beliefs and no profitable deviation after any history. Lemmas 1-3 characterize follower reading and purchase behavior and pooling price equilibria; Propositions 1 and 2 then characterize celebrity and microinfluencer endorsement policies.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Stage 1: the influencer publicly chooses a binding policy to endorse all products or only high-quality products. Stage 2: Nature draws quality, observed by the seller and influencer; if the draw is excluded by the policy, the game ends, otherwise a fixed payment proportionally splits expected endorsement profit. Stage 3: the seller sets first-period price P_1. Stage 4: early followers read the post, choose whether to buy, observe their own fit after purchase, and leave comments.
